items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: where Cottrell and Papa French money, you never made tips there

ctx.x: I never made no tips though. Only, only halls I made tips was, uh, was, uh, Hanson Nagel, and the Rays in Ivorville, Harry Parker, uh, Saratoga, uh, Saratoga and, uh, Ivorville. Billy Phillips was on, uh, Saratoga near the next corner of, uh, uh, uh, uh, more near Benville.

What about, did you ever go to Dixieland, ever play at Dixieland Hall in late years? No? You never played there? I thought maybe you'd make some tips. You know, I'm talking about where Cottrell and Papa French money, you never made tips there. No. No.

Well, it's funny. I would think that, you know, you'd make some good money at Jean Zami or Frantz Zami, but the band didn't get the tips? No, no, we, uh, we had a study, uh, uh, uh, stipulated price, you know. You're regular sound. They had a fixed, they had a fixed price, and the leader would charge them so much for the band. Uh-huh. And that's all. When we had so many hours to play, and that's all. When we start the playing, when it's time to knock off, we knock off, and they pay us off. No tips. There are…
